vts_boundary_basis: NN 52/2025 art. 93(12): the VTS area covers Croatian internal waters, territorial sea and exclusive economic zone; art. 101(2): the VTS service supervises the IMO-adopted routeing and TSS in the Adriatic. Pass 4 overlay against the 1968 Italy-Yugoslavia continental shelf line (points 7 to 17), which Croatia's EEZ limit towards Italy follows: every vertex of the eastern part (positions 4a-4d, 5a-5b, 6a-6b) lies about 6 to 17 NM east of the line, i.e. on the Croatian side; the western part lies mainly on the Italian side (separation zone and southbound lane 3 to 13 NM west), with only the outer edge of its northbound lane (9a, 9b) about 0.6 to 0.8 NM east of the line. IMO structure (COLREG.2/Circ.54 annex 3; HHI notice 11/2004) groups the eastern and western parts under 'In the North Adriatic Sea', with the approaches to the Gulfs of Trieste and Venice as separate schemes (B-III/9, B-III/10), consistent with B-III/8 comprising both parts. The Venice VTS users' manual states the North Adriatic TSS is not inside the Venice VTS area.

tss_name: At the approaches to Puerto Cristobal
vts_boundary_basis: No official source defines a VTS area that includes this TSS. Under ACP N-2-2026 (Z2-S6), Cristobal Signal Station coordinates anchorage entry/exit and harbour movements, and vessels must call it at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater. N-2-2026 does not name the TSS or call the station a VTS. ACP's Enhanced Vessel Traffic Management System (Z2-S7) is a scheduling and information database with no stated service area. NGA Pub. 148 (Z2-S8, Tier 3) says the Panama Canal VTMS 'covers the approaches to Colon and its terminals' but gives no boundary. Coverage of the TSS lanes (about 09°28'N to 09°43'N) is not established.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system applies (the only Part I system in the region is GALREP, VRS-0019). COLREG.2/Circ.65 Annex 2 attaches no reporting. ACP N-2-2026 requires a VHF Ch 12 call to Cristobal Signal Station at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater, plus a continuous Ch 12 watch (vessels of 300 GT or more, 100 GT or more with passengers for hire, commercial towing vessels of 8 m or more) until an ACP pilot takes control. That is canal and anchorage arrival reporting, not a separate MRS. The call point lies about 8 NM north of the breakwater, near the inner (southern) end of the TSS, where the inner lane points are at 09°31'N to 09°32.7'N. The breakwater position is not from an official source. NGA Pub. 148 gives different call distances (6 NM and 12 NM), but the current ACP notice takes precedence.
evidence_summary: IMO B-IX/19, adopted by COLREG.2/Circ.65 (MSC 93) and implemented 1 Dec 2014, with inshore traffic zones on both sides. ACP N-2-2026 (1 Jan 2026) makes Cristobal Signal Station the point of contact at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater and has it coordinate anchorage and harbour movements. It is called a signal station, not a VTS, and the notice does not refer to the TSS. NGA Pub. 148 describes a Panama Canal VTMS 'covering the approaches to Colon' without limits. No Part I MRS applies, and the ACP arrival call is canal arrival reporting. This matches the project treatment of TSS-0176 (Gulf of Panama, Flamenco Signal Station).
source_date: COLREG.2/Circ.65 23 May 2014; ACP N-2-2026 and N-3-2026 1 Jan 2026; NGA Pub. 148 19th Ed 2025 (updated 4 Sep 2026)
unresolved_issue: It is not known whether ACP (or AMP) operates a VTS-designated service, with a defined area, that includes the Atlantic TSS lanes. NGA's statement that the VTMS 'covers the approaches to Colon' is unbounded and Tier 3 only. The official breakwater position and the exact 8 NM point relative to the scheme are unverified. There is no official list of Panamanian VTS. N-1-2026 (Vessel Requirements) could not be retrieved; the URL returned HTML.

vts_boundary_basis: No VTS established. The IMO instruments name MRCC Las Palmas (Salvamento Marítimo) only as a Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre receiving CANREP reports and voluntary TSS notifications (Z3-S3, Z3-S4). An official press release (Z3-S9) says CCS Las Palmas carries out traffic monitoring, and a media report (Z3-S10) says the CCS 'controlled' ships transiting the TSS, but no official source was found that designates a VTS or defines a VTS area covering the TSS. The Las Palmas / Santa Cruz de Tenerife port VTS cover port waters only (not checked in detail; lead only).
reporting_scheme_name: CANREP (Mandatory ship reporting system for the Canary Islands)
reporting_authority: Salvamento Marítimo: MRCC Las Palmas (entry east of 015°30'W) / MRCC Tenerife (entry west of 015°30'W)
reporting_boundary_basis: CANREP area is a polygon (points A-N) along the outer limit of the territorial sea around the archipelago (MSC.213(81) para 2.1). Plotting the COLREG.2/Circ.57 coordinates shows all Eastern TSS points inside the polygon; its northern termination (points 3 and 11-12 at about 28°20'N, on the line CANREP D-E) lies on the CANREP boundary line within 0.05', and the polygon vertex used for the TSS's inshore traffic zone coincides with a CANREP vertex, so the TSS lies within the reporting area. Applies only to tankers of 600 dwt and above carrying heavy crude, heavy fuel oil, bitumen or tar.
evidence_summary: Inside VRS-0023 CANREP (MSC.213(81), in force 1 Dec 2006) by coordinate check; mandatory only for heavy-grade oil tankers of 600 dwt and above. MRCC Las Palmas is an MRCC, not a designated VTS; traffic monitoring of the TSS by Salvamento Marítimo is reported but no VTS designation or VTS area was found.

Pass 4: Salvamento Maritimo reportedly says its Las Palmas and Tenerife centres 'controlled' ships in the TSS in 2025; its website was unreachable, so a Spanish coastal VTS designation is not fully ruled out (lead).
